what: The props shadow ledger (tools/props_ledger.js, README "Player props"): the props model's call on every player in every game to come, frozen at tip-off and graded after the final against DraftKings' closing main lines, beside DraftKings' fair chance. The page shows the model as on trial until the bar is passed.

bar.sample: the first 30,000 graded lines that went over or under (a push drops out), in the order they were graded (data/props_shadow_lines.csv's order: games by grading run, then tip-off, then game id; within a game by player id and stat)
pass_if: log loss: the model's chance of the Over minus DraftKings' fair chance (the whole margin on the Over, 1 - implied(Under)), chances clipped to 1e-6: its bootstrap 90% interval wholly below 0 (10,000 resamples of the games in the sample, seed 0, the 5th to 95th percentile of the resampled mean difference)
Brier score: the same, its interval wholly below 0

flat one-unit bets on the side whose model chance is 3 points or more above the chance its closing price implies (the margin left in), at that price, are up in units on those lines (more than 0; no bets is not up)
bar.otherwise: FAIL: the calls stop (lines already frozen are still graded), and the page never puts a prop in a suggestion or says "model says" or "edge" on one
bar.if_pass: PASS makes the model a candidate to be shown as more than on trial, by a change of its own; nothing on the page moves by itself
bar.before: no verdict before 30,000: until then the summary gives the running numbers and how many of the 30,000 are in, never a verdict or a word of passing

summary.standing: 344 of 30000 graded lines toward the verdict; the bar is judged at 30000, not before
